requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation IS used to await a specific message on an incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The trigger operation is used to await a specific message on an incoming port queue.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `trigger` ["(" TemplateInstance ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`value` (ValueRef | "(" {ValueRef [":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] FieldOrTypeReference] [","]} ")")] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index value` ValueRef]].
requirements.original:
[ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." trigger
  [ "(" TemplateInstance ")" ] 
  [ from Address ]
  [ "->" [ value ( ValueRef| 
          ( "(" { ValueRef[ ":=" [ @decoded [ "(" Expression ")" ] ]
                 FieldOrTypeReference ][","] } ")" )
          ) ]
   [ sender ValueRef] 
   [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue.
requirements.original: The trigger operation removes the top message from the associated incoming port queue.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.condition: the top message meets the matching criteria
requirements.canonical: If the top message of the incoming port queue meets the matching criteria, the `trigger` operation behaves in the same manner as a `receive` operation.
requirements.original: If that top message meets the matching criteria, the trigger operation behaves in the same manner as a receive operation.

requirements.subject: ent:message
requirements.condition: the top message does not fulfil the matching criteria
requirements.canonical: If the top message of the incoming port queue does not fulfil the matching criteria of a `trigger` operation, the message SHALL be removed from the queue without any further action.
requirements.original: If that top message does not fulfil the matching criteria, it shall be removed from the queue without any further action.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation SHALL specify the port name and matching criteria for type and value.
requirements.original: The trigger operation requires the port name, matching criteria for type and value, an optional from restriction (i.e. selection of communication partner) and an optional assignment of the matching message and sender component to variables.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says matching criteria are required, but clause 'Trigger on any message' allows a trigger without argument list. Chosen reading: the matching criteria are required unless the trigger on any message form is used.
readings: A `trigger` operation SHALL always specify matching criteria for type and value.
A `trigger` operation SHALL specify matching criteria for type and value unless it is a trigger on any message without argument list.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation MAY contain an optional `from` restriction selecting the communication partner.
requirements.original: The trigger operation requires the port name, matching criteria for type and value, an optional from restriction (i.e. selection of communication partner) and an optional assignment of the matching message and sender component to variables.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation MAY contain an optional assignment of the matching message and the sender component to variables.
requirements.original: The trigger operation requires the port name, matching criteria for type and value, an optional from restriction (i.e. selection of communication partner) and an optional assignment of the matching message and sender component to variables.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria defined in clause 22.2.2 apply also to the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: The matching criteria as defined in clause 22.2.2 apply also to the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: In the case of one-to-many connections, the `trigger` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: In the case of one-to-many connections the trigger operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The restriction of a `trigger` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted using the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:one-to-one-connection
requirements.canonical: A one-to-one connection IS a simple case of a one-to-many connection and allows the usage of the `from` clause in a `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-on-any-message
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation with no template instance SHALL trigger on the receipt of any message.
requirements.original: A trigger operation with no argument list shall trigger on the receipt of any message.

ambiguity.issue: 'argument list' is used for the optional TemplateInstance of the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-on-any-message
requirements.canonical: A `trigger` operation with no template instance IS identical in meaning to `receive` any message.
requirements.original: Thus, its meaning is identical to the meaning of receive any message.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: The `any port` keywords MAY be used in a `trigger` operation to trigger on a message at any port.
requirements.original: To trigger on a message at any port, use the any port keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The `any from` PortArrayRef syntax MAY be used in a `trigger` operation to trigger on a message at any port of a specific port array.
requirements.original: To trigger on a message at any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` `trigger` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To trigger on a message at any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index of the port of a single-dimensional port array at which the `trigger` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type `integer`.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index of the port of a multi-dimensional port array at which the `trigger` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or `record of integer` variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array
requirements.canonical: When a `trigger` operation checks a port array for matching messages, the iteration over the port indices IS from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching messages, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array
requirements.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the iteration over the ports IS from innermost to outermost array dimension and from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all criteria causes the `trigger` operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:message
requirements.condition: a port in the port array contains a non-matching message
requirements.canonical: If any port of the port array checked for matching contains a message that does not match, the `trigger` operation removes this message.
requirements.original: If any port in the port array which is checked for matching contains a message that does not match, this message is removed and the containing alt statement is re-evaluated, regardless of whether or not other ports in the port array would meet the trigger criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: a port in the port array contains a non-matching message
requirements.canonical: If any port of the port array checked for matching contains a message that does not match, the containing `alt` statement is re-evaluated regardless of whether other ports in the port array would meet the trigger criteria.
requirements.original: If any port in the port array which is checked for matching contains a message that does not match, this message is removed and the containing alt statement is re-evaluated, regardless of whether or not other ports in the port array would meet the trigger criteria.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation CAN be used as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.
requirements.original: The trigger operation can be used as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.

requirements.subject: ent:stand-alone-trigger-statement
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone `trigger` statement IS shorthand for an `alt` statement with two alternatives, one expecting the message and one consuming all other messages and repeating the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: In this latter case the trigger operation is considered to be shorthand for an alt statement with two alternatives (one alternative expecting the message and another alternative consuming all other messages and repeating the alt statement, see ETSI ES 201 873-4 [1]).

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The rules of clause 22.2.2 for storing the received message, parts of the received message or the sender SHALL apply to the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: Rules in clause 22.2.2 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.canonical: The `trigger` operation SHALL only be used on message-based ports.
requirements.original: a) The trigger operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the value to be received shall be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The type of the value to be received by a `trigger` operation SHALL be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.
requirements.original: a) The trigger operation shall only be used on message-based ports and the type of the value to be received shall be included in the list of incoming types of the port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-on-any-message
requirements.canonical: A message received by a trigger on any message SHALL NOT be assigned to a variable.
requirements.original: b) A message received by TriggerOnAnyMessage shall not be assigned to a variable.

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value in a `trigger` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: c) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the sender in a `trigger` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: c) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the types in the receive part are not compatible with the types in the assignment part.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the `from` clause is missing but the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.
requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.
requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:address-ref
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array-ref
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of a `trigger` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: e) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of a `trigger` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection used for single-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the port array.
requirements.original: g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional port arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection used for multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the port array.
requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

ambiguity.issue: 'the dimension of the respective array' is read as the number of dimensions (supported by example 5: p[10][10] with v_i[2]).
readings: The size of the integer array SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the port array.
The size of the integer array SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: index redirection used for multi-dimensional port array
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL allow storing the highest index of all dimensions of the port array.
requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is lazy or fuzzy
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `trigger` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable IS equal to the result produced by the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.canonical: Later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable assigned in a `trigger` operation redirect SHALL NOT lead to repeated invocation of the `trigger` operation.
requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the trigger operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the trigger operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: both from and sender clause present
requirements.canonical: If a `trigger` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the AddressRef in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: j) If the trigger operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

ambiguity.issue: 'template in the from clause' is used although the from clause contains AddressRef items (address or component references), not templates.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: k) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of a data type.
requirements.original: l) TemplateInstance shall be of a data type.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `trigger` statements.
requirements.original: m) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone trigger statements.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that invokes a procedure call.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:getcall-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getcall` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that accepts a procedure call from a remote entity.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:reply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `reply` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that replies to a procedure call from a remote entity.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:raise-operation
requirements.canonical: The `raise` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that raises an exception to an accepted call.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that handles the response from a previous call.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that catches an exception from the called entity.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**

requirements.subject: ent:check-operation
requirements.canonical: The `check` operation IS the procedure-based communication operation that checks whether a call, exception or reply has been received.
requirements.original: **Communication operation** **Keyword** Invoke procedure call **call** Accept procedure call from remote entity **getcall** Reply to procedure call from remote entity **reply** Raise exception (to an accepted call) **raise** Handle response from a previous call **getreply** Catch exception (from called entity) **catch** Check call/exception/reply received **check**
